Pure predicate — one question over a token list, no I/O and no state. It is called before every command in 5 modules (9 call sites), so a log_operation() here would record 'a help flag was looked for' on every single invocation and drown the operations log in non-events; it would also make the help gate depend on the JSON layer it is meant to run ahead of. The callers that ACT on the answer already log what they did. Same file, same call and same reasoning as @drone, @trigger and @memory carry for their identical helper (DPLAN-0291 rule E, 2026-08-13).

handle_command's True means 'this command was mine', never 'it succeeded' (the module contract in flow.py). The handler calls cli_error() first, which flow.py's resolve_exit turns into exit 2: measured 2026-10-04, `drone @flow create . probe NOSUCHTYPE` exits 2. The failure reaches the caller through the exit code, not the bool (flow's decision, leg 5).

handle_command's True means 'this command was mine', never 'it succeeded' (the module contract in flow.py). Each handler calls error() first, which flow.py's resolve_exit turns into a failing exit code; False would route 'registry' on to the next module and end in 'unknown command' (flow's decision, leg 6).

The exception is the answer, not a failure. 97: os.kill(pid, 0) raising PermissionError means the process exists and belongs to someone else, so alive is the true answer. 160 and 186 (147 and 173 until leg 11's seam moved them): FileNotFoundError on the lock means its holder released it between our create and our read, so stale (take over) is the true answer; every other OSError on those reads re-raises (leg 3) (flow's decision, leg 5).

archive_plan's False means 'not archived' on every path: the move raised, the destination is missing, or the source survived. Its three callers each treat it as a failure: close step 3 ('Archive failed - plan file not moved'), the orphan cleanup ('Failed to move orphaned file'), and process_closed_plans (archive_failed, error_count) (flow's decision, leg 10).

Each False means 'not done' on every path; no success path answers False. save_branch_registry: its callers, auto_close_plan and repoint_plan, log the failure and return False, and the plan is then not reported healed. 434 save_central: its one caller, aggregate_central_impl, logs it and returns False. 601 aggregate_central_impl: the aggregate command prints 'Central plans aggregation failed'; push_to_plans_central now raises it into its own failure (leg 10), and close, create and restore warn on that (flow's decision, leg 10).

route_command's True means 'a module handled this command'. A BrokenPipeError is the reader closing stdout early (`drone @flow list | head`): the command ran and its output was cut by the reader, not failed. False would print 'unknown command' for a known one (flow's decision, leg 5).

(flow, FPLAN-1229) The BrokenPipeError handler is the reader closing stdout early (drone @flow list | head): the command ran and only its output was cut, so True ('a module handled this') is the fact, not a stand-in; the info log records it. A raise or warning would turn a normal pipe into an error; False would print 'unknown command' for a known one.

(flow, FPLAN-1229) Read as a check only because 'aggregate' contains 'gate'. On a registry_lock TimeoutError it returns False, meaning 'not done', never 'passed'; its one caller, handle_command, shows error('Central plans aggregation failed') and exits 2, the timeout text logged. A raise would pass route_command's catch-all and end in 'Unknown command'.

(flow, FPLAN-1229) The BrokenPipeError after a successful listing is the reader closing stdout (drone @flow list | head): the listing succeeded and the reader stopped, so True is the true answer. The error-display pipe in the same function logs at warning and returns False.

(flow, FPLAN-1229) Documented contract: exists() has already confirmed the path; only the exact-spelling check cannot run when the parent cannot be listed, so True is the known answer. A raise would break every location lookup (find_repo_root walks every parent) over a permission quirk on a directory that does exist.

(flow, FPLAN-1229) The fallback itself is logged at warning on the line before; this except covers only the optional audit-log record, which must never take an import down: repo_root runs at import time for many callers. The detector flags the word 'fallback' in the name.

(flow, FPLAN-1229) template_registry.json is rebuilt from templates/ on disk with deterministic prefixes: a corrupt or unreadable file is logged at warning, reseeded, rediscovered and saved once. A raise would block every plan command over a rebuildable file. Limit: a prefix registered by hand to dodge a collision is not rediscovered.

(flow, FPLAN-1229) Pre-creating a type's plan registry is a convenience: load_registry reads an absent file as empty and the first save creates it. A failed pre-create is logged at warning and loses nothing; failing add_type or discovery for it would be worse.

(flow, FPLAN-1229) Each except is the answer, not a failure: PermissionError from os.kill(pid, 0) means alive under another user; FileNotFoundError on the lock means its holder released it (take over); ValueError on the pid means no pid yet, so the lock is aged. Normal contention paths, logged at info; any other OSError re-raises. Same contract as the logged_fallback row.

(flow, FPLAN-1229) plans.central.json is derived data: the push replaces branches, statistics and generated_at wholesale, and aggregate rebuilds the lists from the registries, the source of truth. An unreadable file is rebuilt with a warning logged; a raise would leave a corrupt central in place for good.

(flow, FPLAN-1229) is_plan_file answers None (a sentinel, not a bool) for an unreadable file, logged at warning; every caller reads None as never rename, register or close, and the scan carries on. _fire_event answers False (not handled) on a missing trigger package with a warning, so the scan never counts it as a change. A raise would abort the whole scan over one file.

(flow, FPLAN-1229) A plan-type discovery failure processes fplan_registry.json alone, with a warning. Nothing is lost: other types' closed plans keep processed != True and drain on the next run. A raise would stop FPLAN archiving too over a discovery fault.

(flow, FPLAN-1229) Its one caller, _own_row, finds no row in the empty stand-in, so the plan stays open and nothing is saved; the stand-in can never be written over the real registry. Logged at error naming the file. A raise would abort aggregation of every other branch for one unreadable registry.

(flow, FPLAN-1229) Read as a check because 'aggregate' contains 'gate'. False is its only failure value (success is True): the aggregate command prints 'Central plans aggregation failed' and push_to_plans_central raises it. The logged_fallback row covers the same except.

(flow, FPLAN-1229) Heal isolates each plan type: an unreadable type registry is skipped this run with a warning naming it, while load_registry refuses it loudly (RegistryUnreadableError) on every command path. A raise would only reach heal_registry_doctrine_impl's per-type except and log the same skip.

(flow, FPLAN-1229) Classifier input: False means 'not verified', which sends the seat to the repository check or quarantine, never to a re-attribution. An unverifiable seat must not be trusted, so False is the safe answer, logged at warning. A raise would stop the orphan sweep for every other row.

(flow, FPLAN-1229) A smaller seat index only under-attributes: rows go to quarantine, never to a wrong owner, and registry status shows quarantine. Each skipped source is logged at warning. A raise would block the whole heal over one unreadable registry.
